slides.headline: You do not need to work out *every day*.
slides.body: People who packed their weekly exercise into one or two days had similar health outcomes to those who spread it out.

slides.headline: Risk was lower across *every major condition*.
slides.body: Concentrated weekly activity was linked to lower rates of dying from heart conditions and cancer.

slides.headline: Total weekly minutes matter *more than frequency*.
slides.body: Hitting the recommended movement target was linked to similar long term health, no matter how the days were split.

slides.headline: Fit your exercise *around your schedule*.
slides.body: If work takes over your week, packing your movement into a couple of days is just as well supported by the evidence.

caption: Long term health tracking shows that concentrating your workouts into one or two days is linked to the same health outcomes as spreading them across the whole week.
